newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium investigates troops for crimes in Somalia.
newsitem.headline: Belgium investigates troops for crimes in Somalia.

text.p: The Belgian military court said on Friday it had arrested one soldier and was investigating others over allegations they tortured children while serving with United Nations forces in Somalia in 1993.
The investigations were prompted by pictures and stories printed earlier this month in Belgium's Het Laatste Nieuws newspaper.
"According to these accusations, supported by photographs, the said soldiers did on several occasions mistreat children in the course of operation UNOSOM II," the court said in a statement.
The newspaper pictures showed soldiers, with their faces obscured, holding a Somali youth over a fire and forcing others to eat worms and drink heavily salted water.
The court said the two soldiers pictured roasting the child had been identified and interrogated.
"One of them has been arrested, the other has been conditionally released (the alternative to preventive detention)," the court said.
"The investigation is continuing to identify, interview and eventually confront the different people present in the places and on the dates in the allegations," the statement concluded.
It is not the first time that the Belgian troops who were in Somalia have been accused of human rights abuses.
In August 1993, while they were still in the country, there were allegations that the paratroops had massively understated the number of Somalis they had killed during military operations.

The allegations, by five of the paratroops, also said the 1,000 Belgian troops based in Kismayu in southern Somalia often fired at armed Somali fighters even if they themselves had not come under attack.
